text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Budget passes first Knesset reading.
- Regular security consultations to be held with Russia.
- El Al predicts $100 million loss this year. Tourism fell 8 percent between March and September.
- U.S. worried about sale of Israeli technology to China.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Finance Minister Dan Meridor both lose in budget tug-of-war.
- Central bank: Economy slowed in second and third quarters.
- IDB, Clal face changes after Clal chief executive David Wainshal resigns.
- Bill to invalidate Reform and Conservative conversions here due soon.
GLOBES
- Tower Semi-Conductor rejects purchase offer.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu responds to Gesher faction pressures: Harm to social causes in the budget will be reviewed. Budget passes first reading.
- Convicted spy Jonathan Pollard's family: Activities of his wife Esther hold up his release.
- Former U.S. Secretary of State James Baker says peace with Syria conditioned on full Israeli withdrawal from Golan Heights.
- Far more illegal buildings destroyed in Arab sector than in Jewish sector.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Cabinet ministers: An atmosphere of blackmail; Meridor: I am not quitting.
- Settlements will again be declared national areas of preference.
- "I want to make aliya to Israel," says step-granddaughter of Goebbels.
MAARIV

- Major-General Oren Shahor, head of civilian affairs committee in talks with Palestinians, had series of secret meetings with former ministers Shimon Peres and Yossi Beilin. Unidentified source in Netanyahu's office: "A very serious phenomenon".
- Netanyahu promises Foreign Minister David Levy changes in the budget without Meridor's knowledge.
